newsitem.title: USA: NAACP calls rallies in non-violence campaign.
newsitem.headline: NAACP calls rallies in non-violence campaign.

text.p: The National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People said Tuesday it was launching a national non-violence campaign following the murders of two rap stars and the son of comedian Bill Cosby.
The campaign is to culminate in a "National Day of Non-Violence," on April 4, the civil rights group said.
"NAACP is taking action because we place value on each life, especially those of our youth," NAACP President Kweisi Mfume said in a statement.

Organiser Rev. Jamal Harrison Bryant said the group accelerated and expanded plans for the event after the murders of black rap stars Tupac Shakur and Christopher Wallace, also known as Notorious B.I.G., and of Ennis Cosby.
"The attention of this generation now is focused on the whole violence issue," Bryant said.
The campaign, called "Stop the Violence - Start the Love,' will begin with a rally in New York on March 21 and continue with another in Los Angeles tentatively set for March 27.

Bryant said the two cities were chosen because they represented the hotbeds of reported rivalry in the rap music industry that some have blamed for the deaths of Shakur and Wallace, and because they were a launching pad for trends among young African Americans.
On April 4, he said, some 500 local NAACP youth and college organisations will mark the National Day of Non-Violence with events such as candle-light vigils, rallies and church services.
